master.headline: The infrastructure around the model.
master.lead: Perseus is one local-first platform with three interoperable layers for AI workflows inside the operating boundary: Perseus Context Engine resolves live, bounded context; Perseus Vault retains governed local memory; Perseus Ledger records evidence, authority, and time. The platform is designed for on-premises, disconnected, and controlled-network deployments.
master.problem: AI can produce a plausible answer while losing the state that made it useful. The next operator then has to reconstruct the repository state, prior decision, or evidence trail before work can continue.
master.change: Perseus joins context before action, governed memory across sessions, and evidence after action at the workflow boundary—without claiming to replace the model, mission platform, prime integrator, or approving authority.
master.discussion: Bring one bounded workflow, its data boundary, and the integration surface that needs to be made reviewable; we will define the platform contribution and the right technical conversation.
master.engagement: Engagement posture: start with a bounded workflow, data boundary, and integration surface. Perseus can define a technical path with a prime, mission-system owner, or government technical stakeholder.
contribution_rows: Software factories, resilient C2, and distributed decision workflows where a local context/memory/evidence layer strengthens the mission team.
AI/ML, DevSecOps, RMF evidence, cyber, and enterprise IT workflows where state and provenance stay inside the controlled network.
Mission-system integration where local, reviewable AI connects to sensing, EW, PNT, or related workflows.

cyber-networks.headline: Controlled AI workflows need state and evidence that survive the handoff.
cyber-networks.lead: Perseus combines Perseus Context Engine, Perseus Vault, and Perseus Ledger to keep working context, governed memory, and evidence lineage inside the controlled environment where an AI/ML or DevSecOps workflow runs.
cyber-networks.problem: AI-assisted cyber and DevSecOps workflows often lose the state that made an answer useful: the current repository, ticket, deployment, source commitment, or prior decision. That gap makes review, handoff, and risk acceptance harder.
cyber-networks.change: Perseus Context Engine resolves bounded workflow state before action; Perseus Vault preserves local, time-aware memory; Perseus Ledger can package captured inputs, approvals, actions, and served context for downstream review. Perseus is an evidence layer—not an automated cATO platform.
cyber-networks.discussion: Use the C&N Industry Meeting Request Form for a short conversation about one bounded AI/ML, DevSecOps, or RMF evidence workflow, its data boundary, and the integration surface between the agent and existing tools.
cyber-networks.engagement: Briefing posture: use unclassified, non-sensitive workflow details and define the data boundary and existing control or integration surface.
contribution_rows: Evidence-aware context and governed memory for controlled model-assisted workflows.
Ledger provenance and bounded context envelopes that work alongside control, POA&M, monitoring, and engineering systems.
Local deployment where cloud memory, external telemetry, or opaque state is out of bounds.

c3bm.headline: Make AI-enabled C2 and software delivery reviewable across the handoff.
c3bm.lead: Perseus gives AI-enabled C2 and software-factory workflows a local Perseus Context Engine, Perseus Vault memory, and Perseus Ledger evidence layer that strengthens the mission platform while preserving mission authority.
c3bm.problem: Distributed teams and agents move through repositories, decisions, operational artifacts, and evolving mission context. When state disappears between sessions or handoffs, software-factory work becomes harder to review, re-plan, and trust.
c3bm.change: Perseus Context Engine supplies a bounded starting state, Perseus Vault preserves the working record across sessions, and Perseus Ledger records what was used and what happened. The contribution is intentionally modular so a prime or mission-system owner can retain system authority.
c3bm.discussion: Bring one software-factory, resilient-C2, or distributed-decision workflow, the handoffs that fail today, and the existing integration surface; we will define the bounded platform contribution and the right technical owner.
c3bm.engagement: Engagement posture: identify the software-factory or distributed-decision workflow, then define the modular contribution and the prime or mission-system interface.
contribution_rows: Durable context across agent sessions, repositories, tickets, deployments, and engineering handoffs.
Evidence-backed memory for workflows that must be re-planned, handed off, and reviewed.
A modular contribution that supports a prime-led system while preserving mission-platform authority.

electronic-systems.headline: A local evidence layer around mission-system AI.
electronic-systems.lead: Perseus provides Perseus Context Engine, Perseus Vault, and Perseus Ledger around an AI-enabled mission workflow. A qualified prime or domain partner supplies the mission hardware, embedded inference, and system integration authority.
electronic-systems.problem: Mission-system teams need to know what data an AI assistant saw, what it retained, how current it was, and how a decision can be reviewed without moving the working record outside the program boundary.
electronic-systems.change: Perseus Context Engine renders bounded mission context, Perseus Vault retains local and time-aware memory, and Perseus Ledger records evidence and authority boundaries. These three Perseus layers form an inspectable support layer while the mission owner retains hardware, safety, and authorization responsibility.
electronic-systems.discussion: Bring a specific sensing, EW, PNT, or mission-system integration boundary, its deployment constraints, and the prime or technical partner role that owns hardware and test authority.
electronic-systems.engagement: Engagement posture: identify the sensing, EW, PNT, or mission-system boundary and the partner role that owns hardware, safety, and test authority.
contribution_rows: Context and evidence support where local AI must remain close to the mission workflow.
Governed memory, temporal state, and provenance without requiring a cloud memory service.
A bounded infrastructure contribution for the prime, integrator, or domain performer that owns mission hardware and test authority.
